body.heading: Find the buds
paragraphs: In early spring, trees may look bare and asleep. Look closely at the ends of the twigs. There you will find buds — small, tight parcels wrapped in scales.
Inside each bud is a baby leaf or flower, folded up small and kept safe all winter. The scales are its winter coat.

body.heading: Choose your bud
paragraphs: Pick one bud you can visit often, on a low branch near your home. Draw it in your notebook exactly as it looks today.
Buds come in different shapes. Some are fat and round, some are thin and pointy. Different trees make different buds, just like different leaves.

body.heading: Watch it wake
paragraphs: Visit your bud every few days. One warm day, the scales will split and a crumpled green leaf will push out and unfold.
You watched a whole leaf hiding in something smaller than your fingernail. Spring was inside that bud all along.

takeaway: A bud is a folded-up leaf or flower in a winter coat, and watching one open is watching spring arrive.
materials: A magnifying glass if you have one
safetyNotes: Look at buds on the tree — never snap twigs off. Some plants are prickly, so let an adult check the branch first.
screenFreeExtension: Draw the same bud every few days and make a little flip book of it opening.
